cards.back: the breakaway Congress legislators played an important role in installing non-Congress governments in three States - Haryana, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.
cards.quote: the breakaway Congress legislators played an important role in installing non-Congress governments in three States - Haryana, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: Who achieved the floor crossing that gave rise to the phrase "Aya Ram, Gaya Ram"?
cards.back: The expression originated in an amazing feat of floor crossing achieved by Gaya Lal, an MLA in Haryana, in 1967.
cards.quote: The expression originated in an amazing feat of floor crossing achieved by Gaya Lal, an MLA in Haryana, in 1967.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: How many times did Gaya Lal change his party, and in what time?
cards.back: He changed his party thrice in a fortnight, from Congress to United Front, back to Congress and then within nine hours to United Front again!
cards.quote: He changed his party thrice in a fortnight, from Congress to United Front, back to Congress and then within nine hours to United Front again!

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: What was done later to prevent defections?
cards.back: Later, the Constitution was amended to prevent defections.
cards.quote: Later, the Constitution was amended to prevent defections.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: What did the "Kamaraj plan" of 1963 propose?
cards.back: in 1963 he proposed that all senior Congressmen should resign from office to make way for younger party workers
cards.quote: in 1963 he proposed that all senior Congressmen should resign from office to make way for younger party workers

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: What was the Syndicate in the Congress party?
cards.back: Syndicate was the informal name given to a group of Congress leaders who were in control of the party's organisation.
cards.quote: Syndicate was the informal name given to a group of Congress leaders who were in control of the party's organisation.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: Who led the Syndicate, and which State leaders did it include?
cards.back:
K. Kamraj
S. K. Patil of Bombay city
S. Nijalingappa of Mysore
N. Sanjeeva Reddy of Andhra Pradesh
Atulya Ghosh of West Bengal
cards.quote: It was led by K. Kamraj, former Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu and then the president of the Congress party. It included powerful State leaders like S. K. Patil of Bombay city (later named as Mumbai), S. Nijalingappa of Mysore (later Karnataka), N. Sanjeeva Reddy of Andhra Pradesh and Atulya Ghosh of West Bengal.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: To whom did Lal Bahadur Shastri and later Indira Gandhi owe their position?
cards.back: Both Lal Bahadur Shastri and later Indira Gandhi owed their position to the support received from the Syndicate.
cards.quote: Both Lal Bahadur Shastri and later Indira Gandhi owed their position to the support received from the Syndicate.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: How did Indira Gandhi turn her struggle with the Syndicate into an ideological one?
cards.back: Indira Gandhi adopted a very bold strategy. She converted a simple power struggle into an ideological struggle. She launched a series of initiatives to give the government policy a Left orientation.
cards.quote: Indira Gandhi adopted a very bold strategy. She converted a simple power struggle into an ideological struggle. She launched a series of initiatives to give the government policy a Left orientation.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: When did the Congress Working Committee adopt the Ten Point Programme?
cards.back: She got the Congress Working Committee to adopt a Ten Point Programme in May 1967.
cards.quote: She got the Congress Working Committee to adopt a Ten Point Programme in May 1967.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: Ten Point Programme (1 of 2): name the first three items NCERT lists.
cards.back:
social control of banks
nationalisation of General Insurance
ceiling on urban property and income
cards.quote: She got the Congress Working Committee to adopt a Ten Point Programme in May 1967. This programme included social control of banks, nationalisation of General Insurance, ceiling on urban property and income

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: Ten Point Programme (2 of 2): after bank control, insurance and urban ceilings, name the other three items.
cards.back:
public distribution of food grains
land reforms
provision of house sites to the rural poor
cards.quote: public distribution of food grains, land reforms and provision of house sites to the rural poor.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: Whom did the Syndicate nominate as the official Congress candidate in the 1969 Presidential election?
cards.back: Despite Mrs Gandhi's reservations the syndicate managed to nominate her long time opponent and then speaker of the Lok Sabha, N. Sanjeeva Reddy, as the official Congress candidate for the ensuing Presidential elections.
cards.quote: Despite Mrs Gandhi's reservations the syndicate managed to nominate her long time opponent and then speaker of the Lok Sabha, N. Sanjeeva Reddy, as the official Congress candidate for the ensuing Presidential elections.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: Whom did Indira Gandhi encourage to file nomination as an independent candidate in 1969?
cards.back: Indira Gandhi retaliated by encouraging the then Vice-President, V.V. Giri, to file his nomination as an independent candidate.
cards.quote: Indira Gandhi retaliated by encouraging the then Vice-President, V.V. Giri, to file his nomination as an independent candidate.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: Which big popular policy measures did Indira Gandhi announce in 1969?
cards.back: She also announced several big and popular policy measures like the nationalisation of fourteen leading private banks and the abolition of the privy purse or the special privileges given to former princes.
cards.quote: She also announced several big and popular policy measures like the nationalisation of fourteen leading private banks and the abolition of the privy purse or the special privileges given to former princes.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: What happened between Morarji Desai and the Prime Minister over bank nationalisation and the privy purse?
cards.back: On both the above issues serious differences emerged between him and the Prime Minister resulting in Desai leaving the government.
cards.quote: On both the above issues serious differences emerged between him and the Prime Minister resulting in Desai leaving the government.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: What did Congress President S. Nijalingappa do before the 1969 Presidential election?
cards.back: The then Congress President S. Nijalingappa issued a whip asking all the Congress MPs and MLAs to vote in favour of Sanjeeva Reddy, the official candidate of the party.
cards.quote: The then Congress President S. Nijalingappa issued a whip asking all the Congress MPs and MLAs to vote in favour of Sanjeeva Reddy, the official candidate of the party.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: Why was the Indira Gandhi faction known as "requisitionists"?
cards.back: Supporters of Indira Gandhi requisitioned a special meeting of the AICC (that is why this faction came to be known as requisitionists) but this was refused.
cards.quote: Supporters of Indira Gandhi requisitioned a special meeting of the AICC (that is why this faction came to be known as requisitionists) but this was refused.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: What did the Prime Minister call for in the 1969 Presidential election after silently supporting V.V. Giri?
cards.back: After silently supporting V.V. Giri, the Prime Minister openly called for a conscience vote which meant that the MPs and MLAs from the Congress should be free to vote the way they want.
cards.quote: After silently supporting V.V. Giri, the Prime Minister openly called for a conscience vote which meant that the MPs and MLAs from the Congress should be free to vote the way they want.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: Who won the 1969 Presidential election, and who was defeated?
cards.back: The election ultimately resulted in the victory of V.V. Giri, the independent candidate, and the defeat of Sanjeeva Reddy, the official Congress candidate.
cards.quote: The election ultimately resulted in the victory of V.V. Giri, the independent candidate, and the defeat of Sanjeeva Reddy, the official Congress candidate.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: What formalised the split in the Congress in 1969?
cards.back: The defeat of the official Congress candidate formalised the split in the party. The Congress President expelled the Prime Minister from the party; she claimed that her group was the real Congress.
cards.quote: The defeat of the official Congress candidate formalised the split in the party. The Congress President expelled the Prime Minister from the party; she claimed that her group was the real Congress.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: Which two parties emerged from the Congress split of 1969?
cards.back: By November 1969, the Congress group led by the syndicate came to be referred to as the Congress (Organisation) and the group led by Indira Gandhi came to be called the Congress (Requisitionists). These two parties were also described as Old Congress and New Congress.
cards.quote: By November 1969, the Congress group led by the syndicate came to be referred to as the Congress (Organisation) and the group led by Indira Gandhi came to be called the Congress (Requisitionists). These two parties were also described as Old Congress and New Congress.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: How did Indira Gandhi project the 1969 split?
cards.back: Indira Gandhi projected the split as an ideological divide between socialists and conservatives, between the pro-poor and the pro-rich.
cards.quote: Indira Gandhi projected the split as an ideological divide between socialists and conservatives, between the pro-poor and the pro-rich.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: From which year did the Congress begin shedding its character as an umbrella party?
cards.back: Since 1969, the Congress party had starting shedding its character as an umbrella party which accommodated leaders and workers of different ideological dispensations and view points.
cards.quote: Since 1969, the Congress party had starting shedding its character as an umbrella party which accommodated leaders and workers of different ideological dispensations and view points.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: What was the privy purse?
cards.back: the then rulers families would be allowed to retain certain private property, and given a grant in heredity or government allowance, measured on the basis of the extent, revenue and potential of the merging state. This grant was called the privy purse.
cards.quote: the then rulers families would be allowed to retain certain private property, and given a grant in heredity or government allowance, measured on the basis of the extent, revenue and potential of the merging state. This grant was called the privy purse.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: How did Morarji Desai describe the move to abolish privy purses?
cards.back: Morarji Desai, however, called the move morally wrong and amounting to a breach of faith with the princes.
cards.quote: Morarji Desai, however, called the move morally wrong and amounting to a breach of faith with the princes.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: What happened to the 1970 attempt to abolish the privy purse?
cards.back: The government tried to bring a Constitutional amendment in 1970, but it was not passed in Rajya Sabha. It then issued an ordinance which was struck down by the Supreme Court.
cards.quote: The government tried to bring a Constitutional amendment in 1970, but it was not passed in Rajya Sabha. It then issued an ordinance which was struck down by the Supreme Court.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: When was the Constitution amended to remove legal obstacles to abolishing the privy purse?
cards.back: Following its massive victory in the 1971 election, the Constitution was amended to remove legal obstacles for abolition of privy purse.
cards.quote: Following its massive victory in the 1971 election, the Constitution was amended to remove legal obstacles for abolition of privy purse.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: Which parties gave issue-based support to the Indira Gandhi government after the Congress split?
cards.back: The split in the Congress reduced Indira Gandhi Government to a minority. Yet her government continued in office with the issue-based support of a few other parties including the Communist Party of India and the DMK.
cards.quote: The split in the Congress reduced Indira Gandhi Government to a minority. Yet her government continued in office with the issue-based support of a few other parties including the Communist Party of India and the DMK.

source.section: The 1971 Election and Restoration of Congress

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: When did the Indira Gandhi government recommend dissolution of the Lok Sabha?
cards.back: Indira Gandhi's government recommended the dissolution of the Lok Sabha in December 1970.
cards.quote: Indira Gandhi's government recommended the dissolution of the Lok Sabha in December 1970.

source.section: The 1971 Election and Restoration of Congress

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: When were the fifth general elections to the Lok Sabha held?
cards.back: The fifth general election to Lok Sabha were held in February 1971.
cards.quote: The fifth general election to Lok Sabha were held in February 1971.

source.section: The 1971 Election and Restoration of Congress

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: What was the Grand Alliance of 1971?
cards.back: all the major non-communist, non-Congress opposition parties formed an electoral alliance known as the Grand Alliance.
cards.quote: all the major non-communist, non-Congress opposition parties formed an electoral alliance known as the Grand Alliance.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: Name the parties that formed the Grand Alliance of 1971.
cards.back:
Samyukta Socialist Party (SSP)
Praja Socialist Party (PSP)
Bharatiya Jana Sangh (BJS)
Swatantra Party (SWA)
Bharatiya Kranti Dal (BKD)
cards.quote: The Samyukta Socialist Party (SSP), Praja Socialist Party (PSP), Bharatiya Jana Sangh (BJS), Swatantra Party (SWA) and the Bharatiya Kranti Dal (BKD) came together under this umbrella.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: With which party did the ruling Congress(R) ally in the 1971 elections?
cards.back: The ruling party had an alliance with the Communist Party of India (CPI).
cards.quote: The ruling party had an alliance with the Communist Party of India (CPI).

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: What were the rival slogans of the opposition alliance and Indira Gandhi in 1971?
cards.back: Indira Gandhi said that the opposition alliance had only one common programme: Indira Hatao (Remove Indira). In contrast to this, she put forward a positive programme captured in the famous slogan: Garibi Hatao (Remove Poverty).
cards.quote: Indira Gandhi said that the opposition alliance had only one common programme: Indira Hatao (Remove Indira). In contrast to this, she put forward a positive programme captured in the famous slogan: Garibi Hatao (Remove Poverty).

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: Name the focus areas of the Garibi Hatao programme.
cards.back:
growth of the public sector
imposition of ceiling on rural land holdings and urban property
removal of disparities in income and opportunity
abolition of princely privileges
cards.quote: She focused on the growth of the public sector, imposition of ceiling on rural land holdings and urban property, removal of disparities in income and opportunity, and abolition of princely privileges.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: Which groups did Indira Gandhi try to build a support base among through Garibi Hatao?
cards.back: Through garibi hatao Indira Gandhi tried to generate a support base among the disadvantaged, especially among the landless labourers, Dalits and Adivasis, minorities, women and the unemployed youth.
cards.quote: Through garibi hatao Indira Gandhi tried to generate a support base among the disadvantaged, especially among the landless labourers, Dalits and Adivasis, minorities, women and the unemployed youth.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: How many seats and what vote share did the Congress(R)-CPI combine win in 1971?
cards.back: The combine won 375 seats in Lok Sabha and secured 48.4 per cent votes. Indira Gandhi's Congress(R) won 352 seats with about 44 per cent of the popular votes on its own.
cards.quote: The combine won 375 seats in Lok Sabha and secured 48.4 per cent votes. Indira Gandhi's Congress(R) won 352 seats with about 44 per cent of the popular votes on its own.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: How did the Congress(O) perform in the 1971 Lok Sabha elections?
cards.back: Contrast this with the performance of the Congress(O): the party with so many stalwarts could get less than one-fourth of the votes secured by Indira Gandhi's party and win merely 16 seats.
cards.quote: Contrast this with the performance of the Congress(O): the party with so many stalwarts could get less than one-fourth of the votes secured by Indira Gandhi's party and win merely 16 seats.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: How did the Grand Alliance fare in 1971?
cards.back: The Grand Alliance of the opposition proved a grand failure. Their combined tally of seats was less than 60.
cards.quote: The Grand Alliance of the opposition proved a grand failure. Their combined tally of seats was less than 60.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: What did the 1971 result establish for the Congress led by Indira Gandhi?
cards.back: With this the Congress party led by Indira Gandhi established its claim to being the real Congress and restored to it the dominant position in Indian politics.
cards.quote: With this the Congress party led by Indira Gandhi established its claim to being the real Congress and restored to it the dominant position in Indian politics.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: What happened to the Congress in the State Assembly elections held in 1972?
cards.back: Her party swept through all the State Assembly elections held in 1972.
cards.quote: Her party swept through all the State Assembly elections held in 1972.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: What restored the dominance of the Congress in the early 1970s?
cards.back: With two successive election victories, one at the centre and other at the State level, the dominance of the Congress was restored.
cards.quote: With two successive election victories, one at the centre and other at the State level, the dominance of the Congress was restored.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
cards.front: Was the Congress system restored in 1971-72 as a revival of the old Congress party?
cards.back: What Indira Gandhi had done was not a revival of the old Congress party. In many ways she had re-invented the party.
cards.quote: What Indira Gandhi had done was not a revival of the old Congress party. In many ways she had re-invented the party.

cards.front: Who led the nationwide railway strike of May 1974?
cards.back: The National Coordination Committee for Railwaymen’s Struggle led by George Fernandes gave a call for nationwide strike by all employees of the Railways
cards.quote: The National Coordination Committee for Railwaymen’s Struggle led by George Fernandes gave a call for nationwide strike by all employees of the Railways

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Name the three constitutional issues in the Parliament-judiciary conflict.
cards.back:
Can the Parliament abridge Fundamental Rights?
can the Parliament curtail the right to property by making an amendment?
the Parliament amended the Constitution saying that it can abridge Fundamental Rights for giving effect to Directive Principles.
cards.quote: Can the Parliament abridge Fundamental Rights? The Supreme Court said it cannot. Secondly, can the Parliament curtail the right to property by making an amendment? Again, the Court said that Parliament cannot amend the Constitution in such a manner that rights are curtailed. Thirdly, the Parliament amended the Constitution saying that it can abridge Fundamental Rights for giving effect to Directive Principles. But the Supreme Court rejected this provision also.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What did the Court decide in the Kesavananda Bharati Case about the Constitution and Parliament's power to amend it?
cards.back: In this case, the Court gave a decision that there are some basic features of the Constitution and the Parliament cannot amend these features.
cards.quote: this crisis culminated in the famous Kesavananda Bharati Case. In this case, the Court gave a decision that there are some basic features of the Constitution and the Parliament cannot amend these features.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Who was appointed Chief Justice of India in 1973 by setting aside the seniority of three judges?
cards.back: the government set aside the seniority of three judges and appointed Justice A. N. Ray as the Chief Justice of India.
cards.quote: the government set aside the seniority of three judges and appointed Justice A. N. Ray as the Chief Justice of India.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What did people close to the Prime Minister demand of the judiciary and bureaucracy in the 1970s?
cards.back: People close to the Prime Minister started talking of the need for a judiciary and the bureaucracy ‘committed’ to the vision of the executive and the legislature.
cards.quote: People close to the Prime Minister started talking of the need for a judiciary and the bureaucracy ‘committed’ to the vision of the executive and the legislature.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which judge declared Indira Gandhi's election to the Lok Sabha invalid, and when?
cards.back: On 12 June 1975, Justice Jagmohan Lal Sinha of the Allahabad High Court passed a judgment declaring Indira Gandhi’s election to the Lok Sabha invalid.
cards.quote: On 12 June 1975, Justice Jagmohan Lal Sinha of the Allahabad High Court passed a judgment declaring Indira Gandhi’s election to the Lok Sabha invalid.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Who filed the election petition against Indira Gandhi that led to the Allahabad High Court verdict?
cards.back: This order came on an election petition filed by Raj Narain, a socialist leader and a candidate who had contested against her in 1971.
cards.quote: This order came on an election petition filed by Raj Narain, a socialist leader and a candidate who had contested against her in 1971.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: On what ground did the petition challenge Indira Gandhi's 1971 election?
cards.back: The petition, challenged the election of Indira Gandhi on the ground that she had used the services of government servants in her election campaign.
cards.quote: The petition, challenged the election of Indira Gandhi on the ground that she had used the services of government servants in her election campaign.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What relief did the Supreme Court give Indira Gandhi on 24 June 1975?
cards.back: On June 24, the Supreme Court granted her a partial stay on the High Court order – till her appeal was decided, she could remain an MP but could not take part in the proceedings of the Lok Sabha.
cards.quote: On June 24, the Supreme Court granted her a partial stay on the High Court order – till her appeal was decided, she could remain an MP but could not take part in the proceedings of the Lok Sabha.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Where and when was the massive opposition demonstration held before the Emergency?
cards.back: organised a massive demonstration in Delhi’s Ramlila grounds on 25 June 1975.
cards.quote: organised a massive demonstration in Delhi’s Ramlila grounds on 25 June 1975.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which Article of the Constitution was invoked to declare the Emergency in 1975?
cards.back: the government declared that there was a threat of internal disturbances and therefore, it invoked Article 352 of the Constitution.
cards.quote: the government declared that there was a threat of internal disturbances and therefore, it invoked Article 352 of the Constitution.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: On what grounds could Emergency be declared under Article 352 in 1975?
cards.back: Under the provision of this article the government could declare a state of emergency on grounds of external threat or a threat of internal disturbances.
cards.quote: Under the provision of this article the government could declare a state of emergency on grounds of external threat or a threat of internal disturbances.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What two effects does the proclamation of an emergency have on federal powers and rights?
cards.back:
the federal distribution of powers remains practically suspended and all the powers are concentrated in the hands of the union government
the government also gets the power to curtail or restrict all or any of the Fundamental Rights during the emergency.
cards.quote: Once an emergency is proclaimed, the federal distribution of powers remains practically suspended and all the powers are concentrated in the hands of the union government. Secondly, the government also gets the power to curtail or restrict all or any of the Fundamental Rights during the emergency.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: To which President did the Prime Minister recommend the imposition of Emergency on 25 June 1975?
cards.back: On the night of 25 June 1975, the Prime Minister recommended the imposition of Emergency to President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed.
cards.quote: On the night of 25 June 1975, the Prime Minister recommended the imposition of Emergency to President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: When was the Cabinet informed about the Emergency?
cards.back: The Cabinet was informed about it at a special meeting at 6 a.m. on 26 June, after all this had taken place.
cards.quote: The Cabinet was informed about it at a special meeting at 6 a.m. on 26 June, after all this had taken place.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What is press censorship, as used during the Emergency?
cards.back: Newspapers were asked to get prior approval for all material to be published. This is known as press censorship.
cards.quote: Newspapers were asked to get prior approval for all material to be published. This is known as press censorship.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which two organisations did the government ban during the Emergency?
cards.back: the government banned Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and Jamait-e-Islami.
cards.quote: the government banned Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and Jamait-e-Islami.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What is preventive detention?
cards.back: Under this provision, people are arrested and detained not because they have committed any offence, but on the apprehension that they may commit an offence.
cards.quote: Under this provision, people are arrested and detained not because they have committed any offence, but on the apprehension that they may commit an offence.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What did the Supreme Court constitution bench do in April 1976 on habeas corpus petitions during Emergency?
cards.back: In April 1976, the constitution bench of the Supreme Court over-ruled the High Courts and accepted the government’s plea.
cards.quote: In April 1976, the constitution bench of the Supreme Court over-ruled the High Courts and accepted the government’s plea.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which newspapers protested against censorship by leaving blank spaces?
cards.back: Newspapers like the Indian Express and the Statesman protested against censorship by leaving blank spaces where news items had been censored.
cards.quote: Newspapers like the Indian Express and the Statesman protested against censorship by leaving blank spaces where news items had been censored.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which two writers returned their awards in protest against the Emergency?
cards.back: Kannada writer Shivarama Karanth, awarded with Padma Bhushan, and Hindi writer Fanishwarnath Renu, awarded with Padma Shri, returned their awards in protest against the suspension of democracy.
cards.quote: Kannada writer Shivarama Karanth, awarded with Padma Bhushan, and Hindi writer Fanishwarnath Renu, awarded with Padma Shri, returned their awards in protest against the suspension of democracy.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What did the amendment after the Allahabad High Court ruling declare about elections of PM, President and Vice-President?
cards.back: an amendment was made declaring that elections of Prime Minister, President and Vice-President could not be challenged in the Court.
cards.quote: an amendment was made declaring that elections of Prime Minister, President and Vice-President could not be challenged in the Court.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which amendment passed during the Emergency extended the duration of the legislatures from five to six years?
cards.back: The forty-second amendment was also passed during the Emergency. You have already studied that this amendment consisted of a series of changes in many parts of the Constitution. Among the various changes made by this amendment, one was that the duration of the legislatures in the country was extended from five to six years.
cards.quote: The forty-second amendment was also passed during the Emergency. You have already studied that this amendment consisted of a series of changes in many parts of the Constitution. Among the various changes made by this amendment, one was that the duration of the legislatures in the country was extended from five to six years.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What change did the forty-second amendment make to the duration of legislatures?
cards.back: the duration of the legislatures in the country was extended from five to six years.
cards.quote: the duration of the legislatures in the country was extended from five to six years.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: By how long can elections be postponed during an Emergency?
cards.back: during an Emergency, elections can be postponed by one year.
cards.quote: during an Emergency, elections can be postponed by one year.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What is the first lesson of the Emergency for Indian democracy?
cards.back: Thus, one lesson of Emergency is that it is extremely difficult to do away with democracy in India.
cards.quote: Thus, one lesson of Emergency is that it is extremely difficult to do away with democracy in India.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Now, ‘internal’ Emergency can be proclaimed only on the grounds of ‘____’
cards.back: Now, ‘internal’ Emergency can be proclaimed only on the grounds of ‘armed rebellion’
cards.quote: Now, ‘internal’ Emergency can be proclaimed only on the grounds of ‘armed rebellion’

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Who must now give advice to the President in writing to proclaim Emergency?
cards.back: the advice to the President to proclaim Emergency must be given in writing by the Union Cabinet.
cards.quote: the advice to the President to proclaim Emergency must be given in writing by the Union Cabinet.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What did the Shah Commission Report conclude about the administration and the police?
cards.back: according to the Shah Commission Report, the administration and the police became vulnerable to political pressures.
cards.quote: according to the Shah Commission Report, the administration and the police became vulnerable to political pressures.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: The 1977 elections turned into a ____ on the experience of the Emergency
cards.back: The 1977 elections turned into a referendum on the experience of the Emergency
cards.quote: The 1977 elections turned into a referendum on the experience of the Emergency

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: The opposition fought the election on the slogan of ‘____’.
cards.back: The opposition fought the election on the slogan of ‘save democracy’.
cards.quote: The opposition fought the election on the slogan of ‘save democracy’.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: When did the government decide to hold elections after the Emergency?
cards.back: In January 1977, after eighteen months of Emergency, the government decided to hold elections.
cards.quote: In January 1977, after eighteen months of Emergency, the government decided to hold elections.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which new party did the major opposition parties form on the eve of the 1977 elections?
cards.back: they came together on the eve of the elections and formed a new party, known as the Janata Party.
cards.quote: they came together on the eve of the elections and formed a new party, known as the Janata Party.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Whose leadership did the Janata Party accept?
cards.back: The new party accepted the leadership of Jayaprakash Narayan.
cards.quote: The new party accepted the leadership of Jayaprakash Narayan.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which party did Jagjivan Ram lead after leaving the Congress in 1977?
cards.back: Some other Congress leaders also came out and formed a separate party under the leadership of Jagjivan Ram. This party named as Congress for Democracy, later merged with the Janata Party.
cards.quote: Some other Congress leaders also came out and formed a separate party under the leadership of Jagjivan Ram. This party named as Congress for Democracy, later merged with the Janata Party.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: How many Lok Sabha seats did the Congress win in the 1977 elections?
cards.back: The Congress could win only 154 seats in the Lok Sabha.
cards.quote: The Congress could win only 154 seats in the Lok Sabha.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: The Janata Party and its allies won ____ out of the 542 seats in the Lok Sabha; Janata Party itself won ____ seats
cards.back: The Janata Party and its allies won 330 out of the 542 seats in the Lok Sabha; Janata Party itself won 295 seats
cards.quote: The Janata Party and its allies won 330 out of the 542 seats in the Lok Sabha; Janata Party itself won 295 seats

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What happened to the Congress in the 1977 Lok Sabha elections for the first time since Independence?
cards.back: For the first time since Independence, the Congress party was defeated in the Lok Sabha elections.
cards.quote: For the first time since Independence, the Congress party was defeated in the Lok Sabha elections.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: From which constituencies were Indira Gandhi and Sanjay Gandhi defeated in 1977?
cards.back: Indira Gandhi was defeated from Rae Bareli, as was her son Sanjay Gandhi from Amethi.
cards.quote: Indira Gandhi was defeated from Rae Bareli, as was her son Sanjay Gandhi from Amethi.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Name the three leaders who competed for Prime Minister after the 1977 elections.
cards.back:
Morarji Desai
Charan Singh
Jagjivan Ram
cards.quote: there was stiff competition among three leaders for the post of Prime Minister – Morarji Desai, who was the rival to Indira Gandhi ever since 1966-67; Charan Singh, leader of the Bharatiya Lok Dal and a farmers’ leader from UP; and Jagjivan Ram, who had vast experience as a senior minister in the Congress governments.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Who became Prime Minister after the 1977 elections?
cards.back: Eventually Morarji Desai became the Prime Minister
cards.quote: Eventually Morarji Desai became the Prime Minister

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Why can the Emergency period be called a period of constitutional crisis?
cards.back: The Emergency and the period around it can be described as a period of constitutional crisis because it had its origins in the constitutional battle over the jurisdiction of the Parliament and the judiciary.
cards.quote: The Emergency and the period around it can be described as a period of constitutional crisis because it had its origins in the constitutional battle over the jurisdiction of the Parliament and the judiciary.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: But the elections of 1989 marked the end of what political scientists have called the '____'.
cards.back: But the elections of 1989 marked the end of what political scientists have called the 'Congress system'.
cards.quote: But the elections of 1989 marked the end of what political scientists have called the 'Congress system'.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: How many Lok Sabha seats did the Congress win in 1984 and in 1989?
cards.back: The party that had won as many as 415 seats in the Lok Sabha in 1984 was reduced to only 197 in this election.
cards.quote: The party that had won as many as 415 seats in the Lok Sabha in 1984 was reduced to only 197 in this election.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: When did the Congress come back to power after its 1989 defeat?
cards.back: The Congress improved its performance and came back to power soon after the mid-term elections held in 1991.
cards.quote: The Congress improved its performance and came back to power soon after the mid-term elections held in 1991.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which Congress leader withdrew support from Deve Gowda's United Front Government?
cards.back: Congress leader Sitaram Kesri withdrew the crutches of support from Deve Gowda's United Front Government.
cards.quote: Congress leader Sitaram Kesri withdrew the crutches of support from Deve Gowda's United Front Government.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Who assassinated Rajiv Gandhi in May 1991, and where?
cards.back: He was assassinated by a Sri Lankan Tamil linked to the LTTE when he was on an election campaign tour in Tamil Nadu.
cards.quote: He was assassinated by a Sri Lankan Tamil linked to the LTTE when he was on an election campaign tour in Tamil Nadu.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Whom did the Congress choose as Prime Minister after Rajiv Gandhi's death in 1991?
cards.back: In the elections of 1991, Congress emerged as the single largest party. Following Rajiv Gandhi's death, the party chose Narsimha Rao as the Prime Minister.
cards.quote: In the elections of 1991, Congress emerged as the single largest party. Following Rajiv Gandhi's death, the party chose Narsimha Rao as the Prime Minister.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which two opposite political groups supported the National Front from outside in 1989?
cards.back: The National Front (which itself was an alliance of Janata Dal and some other regional parties) received support from two diametrically opposite political groups: the BJP and the Left Front.
cards.quote: The National Front (which itself was an alliance of Janata Dal and some other regional parties) received support from two diametrically opposite political groups: the BJP and the Left Front.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Who led the National Front Government, and who supported it?
cards.back: The National Front Government lead by V. P. Singh was supported by the Left (represented here by Jyoti Basu) as well as the BJP (represented by L. K. Advani)
cards.quote: The National Front Government lead by V. P. Singh was supported by the Left (represented here by Jyoti Basu) as well as the BJP (represented by L. K. Advani)

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Why did the Congress sit in the opposition after the 1989 elections?
cards.back: Though the Congress was the largest party in the Lok Sabha, it did not have a clear majority and therefore, it decided to sit in the opposition.
cards.quote: Though the Congress was the largest party in the Lok Sabha, it did not have a clear majority and therefore, it decided to sit in the opposition.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What era did the emergence of many parties after 1989 initiate at the Centre?
cards.back: This development initiated an era of coalition governments at the Centre, in which regional parties played a crucial role in forming ruling alliances
cards.quote: This development initiated an era of coalition governments at the Centre, in which regional parties played a crucial role in forming ruling alliances

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which party got a clear majority on its own in the 2014 and 2019 Lok Sabha elections?
cards.back: but in 2014 and 2019 Lok Sabha election, the BJP got clear majority on its own.
cards.quote: but in 2014 and 2019 Lok Sabha election, the BJP got clear majority on its own.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which social groups did the powerful parties and movements of the nineties represent?
cards.back: The nineties also saw the emergence of powerful parties and movements that represented the Dalit and backward castes (Other Backward Classes or OBCs).
cards.quote: The nineties also saw the emergence of powerful parties and movements that represented the Dalit and backward castes (Other Backward Classes or OBCs).

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which parties formed the United Front of 1996, and which party supported it?
cards.back: The United Front was similar to the National Front of 1989 for it included Janata Dal and several regional parties. This time the BJP did not support the government. The United Front government was supported by the Congress.
cards.quote: The United Front was similar to the National Front of 1989 for it included Janata Dal and several regional parties. This time the BJP did not support the government. The United Front government was supported by the Congress.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Why did both the Left and the BJP support the National Front Government in 1989?
cards.back: In 1989, both the Left and the BJP supported the National Front Government because they wanted to keep the Congress out of power.
cards.quote: In 1989, both the Left and the BJP supported the National Front Government because they wanted to keep the Congress out of power.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Why did both the Congress and the Left support the United Front government in 1996?
cards.back: In 1996, the Left continued to support the non-Congress government but this time the Congress, supported it, as both the Congress and the Left wanted to keep the BJP out of power.
cards.quote: In 1996, the Left continued to support the non-Congress government but this time the Congress, supported it, as both the Congress and the Left wanted to keep the BJP out of power.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What happened to the BJP in the 1996 election?
cards.back: It emerged as the largest party in the 1996 election and was invited to form the government.
cards.quote: It emerged as the largest party in the 1996 election and was invited to form the government.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: When did the BJP lead its first coalition government, and when was it re-elected?
cards.back: It finally came to power by leading a coalition government from May 1998 to June 1999 and was re-elected in October 1999.
cards.quote: It finally came to power by leading a coalition government from May 1998 to June 1999 and was re-elected in October 1999.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Who was the Prime Minister during both the NDA governments of 1998 and 1999?
cards.back: Atal Behari Vajpayee was the Prime Minister during both these NDA governments and his government formed in 1999 completed its full term.
cards.quote: Atal Behari Vajpayee was the Prime Minister during both these NDA governments and his government formed in 1999 completed its full term.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Name the coalition governments at the Centre formed with the support of many regional parties, 1989-2009.
cards.back:
National Front in 1989
United Front in 1996 and 1997
BJP-led coalition in 1998
NDA in 1999
UPA in 2004 and 2009
cards.quote: This applied to the National Front in 1989, the United Front in 1996 and 1997, the BJP-led coalition in 1998, the NDA in 1999, the UPA in 2004 and 2009.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Why was the earlier Congress dominance called the 'Congress system'?
cards.back: it was the Congress party itself that was a 'coalition' of different interests and different social strata and groups. This gave rise to the term 'Congress system'.
cards.quote: it was the Congress party itself that was a 'coalition' of different interests and different social strata and groups. This gave rise to the term 'Congress system'.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which party brought together political groups with strong OBC support in the 1980s?
cards.back: In the 1980s, the Janata Dal brought together a similar combination of political groups with strong support among the OBCs.
cards.quote: In the 1980s, the Janata Dal brought together a similar combination of political groups with strong support among the OBCs.

source.section: Political Rise of Other Backward Classes

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: When and by whom was the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) formed?
cards.back: After the fall of the Janata Party and its break-up, the supporters of erstwhile Jana Sangh formed the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in 1980.
cards.quote: After the fall of the Janata Party and its break-up, the supporters of erstwhile Jana Sangh formed the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in 1980.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What ideology did the BJP embrace after its formation in 1980?
cards.back: BJP embraced 'Gandhian' Socialism' along with cultural nationalism as its ideology.
cards.quote: BJP embraced 'Gandhian' Socialism' along with cultural nationalism as its ideology.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What did the BJP begin to emphasise as the core of its ideology after 1986?
cards.back: After 1986, the party began to emphasise nationalism as the core of its ideology.
cards.quote: After 1986, the party began to emphasise nationalism as the core of its ideology.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: In which elections did the combined votes of the Congress and the BJP not add up to more than fifty per cent after 1989?
cards.back: since the 1989 election, the votes polled by the two parties, Congress and the BJP, most of the time, add up to more than fifty per cent except in 1996, 2004 and 2009.
cards.quote: since the 1989 election, the votes polled by the two parties, Congress and the BJP, most of the time, add up to more than fifty per cent except in 1996, 2004 and 2009.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What happened in the 2004 elections, and who supported the new UPA government?
cards.back: The National Democratic Alliance (NDA) was defeated and a new coalition government led by the Congress, known as the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) came to power. This government received support from the Left Front parties.
cards.quote: The National Democratic Alliance (NDA) was defeated and a new coalition government led by the Congress, known as the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) came to power. This government received support from the Left Front parties.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: On which issue did the Left parties withdraw support from the UPA government in July 2008?
cards.back: The Congress led UPA government completed its term despite Left parties withdrawing the support in July 2008 on the issue of Indo-US nuclear deal.
cards.quote: The Congress led UPA government completed its term despite Left parties withdrawing the support in July 2008 on the issue of Indo-US nuclear deal.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: How did the Congress seats in the Lok Sabha change from 2004 to 2009?
cards.back: Results witnessed a rise in the number of seats (from 145 in 2004 to 206 in 2009) of the Indian National Congress (INC) and Congress led UPA Government.
cards.quote: Results witnessed a rise in the number of seats (from 145 in 2004 to 206 in 2009) of the Indian National Congress (INC) and Congress led UPA Government.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Who was sworn as Prime Minister in 2009, heading the UPA coalition again?
cards.back: Dr. Manmohan Singh was sworn as Prime Minister for the second term, heading the coalition government of UPA again.
cards.quote: Dr. Manmohan Singh was sworn as Prime Minister for the second term, heading the coalition government of UPA again.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Whom did the BJP declare as its Prime Ministerial candidate in September 2013?
cards.back: Bhartiya Janata Party declared Narendra Modi (then the Chief Minister of Gujrat) as its Prime Ministerial candidate in September 2013.
cards.quote: Bhartiya Janata Party declared Narendra Modi (then the Chief Minister of Gujrat) as its Prime Ministerial candidate in September 2013.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: How many seats did the BJP win on its own in the 2014 Lok Sabha elections?
cards.back: BJP under the leadership of Narendra Modi got a clear majority in 16th Lok Sabha elections held in 2014. BJP won 282 seats on its own, becoming the first party to gain single party majority after 30 years.
cards.quote: BJP under the leadership of Narendra Modi got a clear majority in 16th Lok Sabha elections held in 2014. BJP won 282 seats on its own, becoming the first party to gain single party majority after 30 years.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: How many seats did the BJP win on its own in the 2019 Lok Sabha election?
cards.back: The BJP again emerged victorious with 303 seats of its own in 2019 Lok Sabha election.
cards.quote: The BJP again emerged victorious with 303 seats of its own in 2019 Lok Sabha election.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What is the third element of the consensus that emerged among most parties after 1989?
cards.back: Third, acceptance of the role of State level parties in governance of the country – the distinction between State level and national level parties is fast becoming less important.
cards.quote: Third, acceptance of the role of State level parties in governance of the country – the distinction between State level and national level parties is fast becoming less important.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What is the fourth element of the consensus that emerged among most parties after 1989?
cards.back: Fourth, emphasis on pragmatic considerations rather than ideological positions and political alliances without ideological agreement – coalition politics has shifted the focus of political parties from ideological differences to power sharing arrangements.
cards.quote: Fourth, emphasis on pragmatic considerations rather than ideological positions and political alliances without ideological agreement – coalition politics has shifted the focus of political parties from ideological differences to power sharing arrangements.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Did most NDA parties agree with the BJP's 'Hindutva' ideology while forming the government?
cards.back: Thus, most parties of the NDA did not agree with the 'Hindutva' ideology of the BJP. Yet, they came together to form a government and remained in power for a full term.
cards.quote: Thus, most parties of the NDA did not agree with the 'Hindutva' ideology of the BJP. Yet, they came together to form a government and remained in power for a full term.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: When was the Berlin Wall built, and when did the people break it?
cards.back: Built in 1961 to separate East Berlin from West Berlin, this more than 150 kilometre long wall stood for 28 years and was finally broken by the people on 9 November 1989.
cards.quote: Built in 1961 to separate East Berlin from West Berlin, this more than 150 kilometre long wall stood for 28 years and was finally broken by the people on 9 November 1989.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: The ____ symbolised the division between the capitalist and the communist world.
cards.back: The Berlin Wall symbolised the division between the capitalist and the communist world.
cards.quote: The Berlin Wall symbolised the division between the capitalist and the communist world.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: The USSR came into being after which revolution, and in which year?
cards.back: The Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR) came into being after the socialist revolution in Russia in 1917.
cards.quote: The Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR) came into being after the socialist revolution in Russia in 1917.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Who was the founder-head of the USSR (1917-1924)?
cards.back: Vladimir Lenin (1870-1924) Founder of the Bolshevik Communist party; leader of the Russian Revolution of 1917 and the founder-head of the USSR during the most difficult period following the revolution (1917-1924)
cards.quote: Vladimir Lenin (1870-1924) Founder of the Bolshevik Communist party; leader of the Russian Revolution of 1917 and the founder-head of the USSR during the most difficult period following the revolution (1917-1924)

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: The Soviet political system centred around the ____, and no other political party or opposition was allowed.
cards.back: The Soviet political system centred around the communist party, and no other political party or opposition was allowed.
cards.quote: The Soviet political system centred around the communist party, and no other political party or opposition was allowed.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: How was the economy run in the Soviet system?
cards.back: The economy was planned and controlled by the state.
cards.quote: The economy was planned and controlled by the state.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What was the Second World (the 'socialist bloc')?
cards.back: After the Second World War, the east European countries that the Soviet army had liberated from the fascist forces came under the control of the USSR. The political and the economic systems of all these countries were modelled after the USSR. This group of countries was called the Second World or the 'socialist bloc'.
cards.quote: After the Second World War, the east European countries that the Soviet army had liberated from the fascist forces came under the control of the USSR. The political and the economic systems of all these countries were modelled after the USSR. This group of countries was called the Second World or the 'socialist bloc'.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which military alliance held the Second World countries together, and who led the bloc?
cards.back: The Warsaw Pact, a military alliance, held them together. The USSR was the leader of the bloc.
cards.quote: The Warsaw Pact, a military alliance, held them together. The USSR was the leader of the bloc.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What was the dominant form of ownership in the Soviet system?
cards.back: State ownership was the dominant form of ownership: land and productive assets were owned and controlled by the Soviet state.
cards.quote: State ownership was the dominant form of ownership: land and productive assets were owned and controlled by the Soviet state.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What two things did the Soviet system become, making life difficult for citizens?
cards.back: bureaucratic and authoritarian
cards.quote: The Soviet system, however, became very bureaucratic and authoritarian, making life very difficult for its citizens.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: How many republics formed the USSR, and which one dominated them in reality?
cards.back: Although, on paper, Russia was only one of the fifteen republics that together constituted the USSR, in reality Russia dominated everything, and people from other regions felt neglected and often suppressed.
cards.quote: Although, on paper, Russia was only one of the fifteen republics that together constituted the USSR, in reality Russia dominated everything, and people from other regions felt neglected and often suppressed.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Who succeeded Lenin and led the USSR (1924-53), beginning rapid industrialisation and forcible collectivisation?
cards.back: Joseph Stalin (1879-1953) Successor to Lenin and led the Soviet Union during its consolidation (1924-53); began rapid industrialisation and forcible collectivisation of agriculture
cards.quote: Joseph Stalin (1879-1953) Successor to Lenin and led the Soviet Union during its consolidation (1924-53); began rapid industrialisation and forcible collectivisation of agriculture

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan in ____ weakened the system even further.
cards.back: The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan in 1979 weakened the system even further.
cards.quote: The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan in 1979 weakened the system even further.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: ____, who had become General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union in ____, sought to reform this system.
cards.back: Mikhail Gorbachev, who had become General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union in 1985, sought to reform this system.
cards.quote: Mikhail Gorbachev, who had become General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union in 1985, sought to reform this system.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Why were reforms necessary in the USSR under Gorbachev?
cards.back: Reforms were necessary to keep the USSR abreast of the information and technological revolutions taking place in the West.
cards.quote: Reforms were necessary to keep the USSR abreast of the information and technological revolutions taking place in the West.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: How did the people of the East European Soviet bloc countries react to Gorbachev's reforms?
cards.back: The people in the East European countries which were part of the Soviet bloc started to protest against their own governments and Soviet control.
cards.quote: The people in the East European countries which were part of the Soviet bloc started to protest against their own governments and Soviet control.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: How did East European communist regimes fare when the USSR under Gorbachev did not intervene in the disturbances?
cards.back: Gorbachev, did not intervene when the disturbances occurred, and the communist regimes collapsed one after another.
cards.quote: Gorbachev, did not intervene when the disturbances occurred, and the communist regimes collapsed one after another.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Who encouraged the 1991 coup in the USSR?
cards.back: Communist Party hardliners
cards.quote: A coup took place in 1991 that was encouraged by Communist Party hardliners.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Who emerged as a national hero in opposing the 1991 coup against Gorbachev?
cards.back: Boris Yeltsin emerged as a national hero in opposing this coup.
cards.quote: Boris Yeltsin emerged as a national hero in opposing this coup.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which three republics declared in December 1991 that the Soviet Union was disbanded?
cards.back: In December 1991, under the leadership of Yeltsin, Russia, Ukraine and Belarus, three major republics of the USSR, declared that the Soviet Union was disbanded.
cards.quote: In December 1991, under the leadership of Yeltsin, Russia, Ukraine and Belarus, three major republics of the USSR, declared that the Soviet Union was disbanded.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What happened to the Communist Party of the Soviet Union after the disbanding, and what was adopted?
cards.back: The Communist Party of the Soviet Union was banned. Capitalism and democracy were adopted as the bases for the post-Soviet republics.
cards.quote: The Communist Party of the Soviet Union was banned. Capitalism and democracy were adopted as the bases for the post-Soviet republics.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which Soviet leader (1953-64) denounced Stalin's style and suggested 'peaceful coexistence' with the West?
cards.back: Nikita Khrushchev (1894-1971) Leader of the Soviet Union (1953-64); denounced Stalin's leadership style and introduced some reforms in 1956; suggested 'peaceful coexistence' with the West
cards.quote: Nikita Khrushchev (1894-1971) Leader of the Soviet Union (1953-64); denounced Stalin's leadership style and introduced some reforms in 1956; suggested 'peaceful coexistence' with the West

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which state was accepted as the successor state of the USSR, and which UN seat did it inherit?
cards.back: Russia was now accepted as the successor state of the Soviet Union. It inherited the Soviet seat in the UN Security Council.
cards.quote: Russia was now accepted as the successor state of the Soviet Union. It inherited the Soviet seat in the UN Security Council.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What did Russia accept and take over as the successor of the USSR?
cards.back: Russia accepted all the international treaties and commitments of the Soviet Union. It took over as the only nuclear state of the post-Soviet space
cards.quote: Russia accepted all the international treaties and commitments of the Soviet Union. It took over as the only nuclear state of the post-Soviet space

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Internal weaknesses of which Soviet institutions, failing the people's aspirations, caused the system's collapse?
cards.back: There is no doubt that the internal weaknesses of Soviet political and economic institutions, which failed to meet the aspirations of the people, were responsible for the collapse of the system.
cards.quote: There is no doubt that the internal weaknesses of Soviet political and economic institutions, which failed to meet the aspirations of the people, were responsible for the collapse of the system.

source.section: Why did the Soviet Union Disintegrate?

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Why did the Soviet system become weak and its economy stagnate?
cards.back: The Soviet economy used much of its resources in maintaining a nuclear and military arsenal and the development of its satellite states in Eastern Europe and within the Soviet system (the five Central Asian Republics in particular). This led to a huge economic burden that the system could not cope with.
cards.quote: The Soviet economy used much of its resources in maintaining a nuclear and military arsenal and the development of its satellite states in Eastern Europe and within the Soviet system (the five Central Asian Republics in particular). This led to a huge economic burden that the system could not cope with.

source.section: Why did the Soviet Union Disintegrate?

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: For how long had the Communist Party ruled the Soviet Union without being accountable to the people?
cards.back: The Communist Party that had ruled the Soviet Union for over 70 years was not accountable to the people.
cards.quote: The Communist Party that had ruled the Soviet Union for over 70 years was not accountable to the people.

source.section: Why did the Soviet Union Disintegrate?

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Name the five reasons ordinary people were alienated from the Soviet system.
cards.back:
slow and stifling administration
rampant corruption
the inability of the system to correct mistakes it had made
the unwillingness to allow more openness in government
the centralisation of authority in a vast land
cards.quote: slow and stifling administration, rampant corruption, the inability of the system to correct mistakes it had made, the unwillingness to allow more openness in government, and the centralisation of authority in a vast land

source.section: Why did the Soviet Union Disintegrate?

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What three things did Gorbachev's reforms promise?
cards.back:
reform the economy
catch up with the West
loosen the administrative system
cards.quote: Gorbachev promised to reform the economy, catch up with the West, and loosen the administrative system.

source.section: Why did the Soviet Union Disintegrate?

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What did Gorbachev set in motion when he loosened the system through his reforms?
cards.back: when Gorbachev carried out his reforms and loosened the system, he set in motion forces and expectations that few could have predicted and became virtually impossible to control.
cards.quote: when Gorbachev carried out his reforms and loosened the system, he set in motion forces and expectations that few could have predicted and became virtually impossible to control.

source.section: Why did the Soviet Union Disintegrate?

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What was the final and most immediate cause of the disintegration of the USSR?
cards.back: The rise of nationalism and the desire for sovereignty within various republics including Russia and the Baltic Republics (Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania), Ukraine, Georgia, and others proved to be the final and most immediate cause for the disintegration of the USSR.
cards.quote: The rise of nationalism and the desire for sovereignty within various republics including Russia and the Baltic Republics (Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania), Ukraine, Georgia, and others proved to be the final and most immediate cause for the disintegration of the USSR.

source.section: Why did the Soviet Union Disintegrate?

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Name the three Baltic republics of the USSR.
cards.back:
Estonia
Latvia
Lithuania
cards.quote: the Baltic Republics (Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania)

source.section: Why did the Soviet Union Disintegrate?

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which Soviet leader (1964-82) is associated with the détente phase with the US?
cards.back: Leonid Brezhnev (1906-82) Leader of the Soviet Union (1964-82); proposed Asian Collective Security system; associated with the détente phase in relations with the US
cards.quote: Leonid Brezhnev (1906-82) Leader of the Soviet Union (1964-82); proposed Asian Collective Security system; associated with the détente phase in relations with the US

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Who was the last leader of the Soviet Union (1985-91)?
cards.back: Mikhail Gorbachev (Born 1931) Last leader of the Soviet Union (1985-91)
cards.quote: Mikhail Gorbachev (Born 1931) Last leader of the Soviet Union (1985-91)

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which two reform policies did Gorbachev introduce, and what do they mean?
cards.back: introduced economic and political reform policies of perestroika (restructuring) and glasnost (openness)
cards.quote: introduced economic and political reform policies of perestroika (restructuring) and glasnost (openness)

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: March 1985: who became General Secretary and who was appointed Communist Party head in Moscow?
cards.back: Mikhail Gorbachev elected as the General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union; appoints Boris Yeltsin as the head of the Communist Party in Moscow
cards.quote: Mikhail Gorbachev elected as the General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union; appoints Boris Yeltsin as the head of the Communist Party in Moscow

source.section: Timeline of Disintegration of the Soviet Union

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: October 1989: what did the Soviet Union declare about the Warsaw Pact members?
cards.back: Soviet Union declares that the Warsaw Pact members are free to decide their own futures; Berlin Wall falls in November
cards.quote: Soviet Union declares that the Warsaw Pact members are free to decide their own futures; Berlin Wall falls in November

source.section: Timeline of Disintegration of the Soviet Union

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: February 1990: what did Gorbachev do to the Communist Party's monopoly on power?
cards.back: Gorbachev strips the Soviet Communist Party of its 72-year-long monopoly on power by calling on the Soviet parliament (Duma) to permit multi-party politics
cards.quote: Gorbachev strips the Soviet Communist Party of its 72-year-long monopoly on power by calling on the Soviet parliament (Duma) to permit multi-party politics

source.section: Timeline of Disintegration of the Soviet Union

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which was the first of the 15 Soviet republics to declare its independence (March 1990)?
cards.back: Lithuania
cards.quote: Lithuania becomes the first of the 15 Soviet republics to declare its independence

source.section: Timeline of Disintegration of the Soviet Union

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: June 1991: who became the President of Russia?
cards.back: Yeltsin, no longer in the Communist Party, becomes the President of Russia
cards.quote: Yeltsin, no longer in the Communist Party, becomes the President of Russia

source.section: Timeline of Disintegration of the Soviet Union

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: August 1991: what happened to the Communist Party hardliners' coup against Gorbachev?
cards.back: The Communist Party hardliners stage an abortive coup against Gorbachev
cards.quote: The Communist Party hardliners stage an abortive coup against Gorbachev

source.section: Timeline of Disintegration of the Soviet Union

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: September 1991: what happened to the three Baltic republics, and when did they join NATO?
cards.back: Three Baltic republics of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania become UN members (later join NATO in March 2004)
cards.quote: Three Baltic republics of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania become UN members (later join NATO in March 2004)

source.section: Timeline of Disintegration of the Soviet Union

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: December 1991: which treaty did Russia, Belarus and Ukraine annul, and what did they establish?
cards.back: Russia, Belarus and Ukraine decide to annul the 1922 Treaty on the Creation of the USSR and establish the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS)
cards.quote: Russia, Belarus and Ukraine decide to annul the 1922 Treaty on the Creation of the USSR and establish the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS)

source.section: Timeline of Disintegration of the Soviet Union

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which eight other republics joined the CIS in December 1991?
cards.back:
Armenia
Azerbaijan
Moldova
Kazakhstan
Kyrgyzstan
Tajikistan
Turkmenistan
Uzbekistan
cards.quote: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Moldova, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan join the CIS

source.section: Timeline of Disintegration of the Soviet Union

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: 25 December 1991: what happened to the Soviet Union?
cards.back: Gorbachev resigns as the President of the Soviet Union; the end of the Soviet Union
cards.quote: Gorbachev resigns as the President of the Soviet Union; the end of the Soviet Union

source.section: Timeline of Disintegration of the Soviet Union

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What was the first enduring change after the collapse of the Second World?
cards.back: First of all, it meant the end of Cold War confrontations.
cards.quote: First of all, it meant the end of Cold War confrontations.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What was the second enduring change after the collapse of the Second World?
cards.back: Second, power relations in world politics changed
cards.quote: Second, power relations in world politics changed

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What two possibilities did the end of the Cold War leave open?
cards.back:
unipolar system
multipolar system
cards.quote: The end of the Cold War left open only two possibilities: either the remaining superpower would dominate and create a unipolar system, or different countries or groups of countries could become important players in the international system, thereby bringing in a multipolar system where no one power could dominate.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: After the end of the Cold War, which country became the sole superpower?
cards.back: As it turned out, the US became the sole superpower.
cards.quote: As it turned out, the US became the sole superpower.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which institutions became powerful advisors to post-communist countries by giving loans for transition to capitalism?
cards.back: Institutions like the World Bank and International Monetary Fund became powerful advisors to all these countries since they gave them loans for their transitions to capitalism.
cards.quote: Institutions like the World Bank and International Monetary Fund became powerful advisors to all these countries since they gave them loans for their transitions to capitalism.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Politically, the notion of ____ emerged as the best way to organise political life.
cards.back: Politically, the notion of liberal democracy emerged as the best way to organise political life.
cards.quote: Politically, the notion of liberal democracy emerged as the best way to organise political life.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What was the third enduring change after the collapse of the Soviet bloc?
cards.back: Third, the end of the Soviet bloc meant the emergence of many new countries.
cards.quote: Third, the end of the Soviet bloc meant the emergence of many new countries.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Which organisations did the Baltic and east European states want to join?
cards.back: Some of them, especially the Baltic and east European states, wanted to join the European Union and become part of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).
cards.quote: Some of them, especially the Baltic and east European states, wanted to join the European Union and become part of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Who was the first elected President of Russia (1991-1999)?
cards.back: Boris Yeltsin (1931-2007) The first elected President of Russia (1991-1999)
cards.quote: Boris Yeltsin (1931-2007) The first elected President of Russia (1991-1999)

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What is 'shock therapy'?
cards.back: The model of transition in Russia, Central Asia and east Europe that was influenced by the World Bank and the IMF came to be known as 'shock therapy'.
cards.quote: The model of transition in Russia, Central Asia and east Europe that was influenced by the World Bank and the IMF came to be known as 'shock therapy'.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What total shift did shock therapy require of each country?
cards.back: Each of these countries was required to make a total shift to a capitalist economy, which meant rooting out completely any structures evolved during the Soviet period.
cards.quote: Each of these countries was required to make a total shift to a capitalist economy, which meant rooting out completely any structures evolved during the Soviet period.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Under shock therapy, what was to be the dominant pattern of property ownership?
cards.back: private ownership
cards.quote: Above all, it meant that private ownership was to be the dominant pattern of ownership of property.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What did shock therapy do to state assets and to collective farms?
